svg.title: Conventions and reading guide. For Φ : Md(C) →Md(C) we use the unnormalized Choi matrix J(Φ) = ∑︁ p,q |p⟩⟨q| ⊗Φ(|p⟩⟨q|). Its rank counts Kraus operators; the complex-linear rank of Φ counts independent image operators. Neither is the internal Hilbert dimension d. The sector-restricted cost D includes the orthogonal current-symbol register, whereas d need not store that symbol internally. All trine-law and seed parameters are dimensionless; no physical time or energy scale is inferred from them. Section 2 establishes the general completion and emitted-symbol interfaces. Sections 3 and 4 give the exact low- and high-noise memory regimes. The remaining sections compare one-step and complete-history costs, then demonstrate access-dependent distinctions between passive-law-equivalent sources. The technical companion retains alternative constructions, approximation statements and additional accounting tasks. The quantum stochastic-realization problem and memory compression have established antecedents [7, 11, 15]; a systematic compression method for nondeterministic quantum implementations is given in Elliott [3]. These works address general realization, representation or memory/thermal questions; they do not by themselves give the particular delayed-trine Kraus and retained-history optima proved here. Normal measurement-model and multi-time resource accounting are established [1, 10]. Our contributions are the stated constructions, exact process-specific bounds and their operational separation. Targeted literature examination does not establish publication priority. Conventional Born probabilities are assumed; no new Born-selection, collapse, consciousness or unique-ontology claim is inferred.
